system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- Evidence text comes from a PDF text layer. If symbols are garbled so that you cannot verify the atom, answer "hold" for that check and say so.
- Be strict. When unsure between pass and a non-pass value, choose the non-pass value and explain.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom. pass = fully stated. revise = the core claim is stated, and the gap is only wording, strength, or a dropped/extra peripheral qualifier that can be fixed by deleting or softening words (say what). fail = not stated, OR the atom adds substantive content the evidence lacks: a scope or population restriction (e.g. 'In B-ALL'), a mechanism or operation, a characterization (e.g. 'an unbounded while loop'), or a formula/definition. If deleting the unsupported part would change what the atom tests, it is fail, not revise. For pass, put the supporting evidence ids in cite (required).
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / revise / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge: one fact a person who studied the concept would simply know. revise = the core fact is recall-level but the sentence carries extra load that must be removed, e.g. stacked conditions (since/although/if ... and ...), a procedural or evaluative add-on ('easy to define but requires checking ...'), or a clause that introduces a second technical concept that must be known separately (e.g. 'if X is an inner Kan complex' when that is not the card concept). fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = the authors' opinion or choice, or the finding of one study, so the answer is not fixed without the source.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a single system, product, or one study's topic.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}
user:
CONCEPT: Minimal fibration
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Minimal ∞-categories, Kan complexes, J-fibrations and the dendroidal version with automorphisms: definition via J-equivalent simplices, rigidity of equivalences, existence of minimal deformation retracts, local triviality, and conditions on stabilizers/normality.

ATOMS:
- HMDEND-C07-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: For a J-fibration $p: X \to S$ between ∞-categories (or a Kan fibration between general simplicial sets), $p$ is a minimal J-fibration (minimal Kan fibration) if any two fibrewise J-equivalent simplices are equal, where fibrewise J-equivalent n-simplices are those that are fibrewise J-homotopic relative to $\partial\Delta[n]$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0224-s06] Definition 5.69 Let p : X →S be a J-fibration between ∞-categories or a Kan fibration between general simplicial sets.
    [HMDEND-p0224-s10] (b) The map p : X →S is a minimal J-fibration (or a minimal Kan fibration if p is
    [HMDEND-p0224-s11] a Kan fibration) if any two fibrewise J-equivalent simplices are equal.
- HMDEND-C07-S1-02.r1 | S1
  ATOM: A map $p : X \to S$ is a minimal J-fibration if for any two fibrewise J-equivalent dendrices $x, y \in X_T$ there exists an automorphism $\alpha$ of $T$ such that $\alpha^*x = y$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0273-s11] (b) The map p : X →S is a minimal J-fibration if for any two fibrewise J-equivalent
    [HMDEND-p0273-s12] dendrices x, y ∈XT, there exists an automorphism α of T so that α∗x = y.
- HMDEND-C07-S1-03.r1a | S1
  ATOM: An ∞-category $X$ is minimal if any two J-equivalent simplices in $X$ are equal.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0218-s03] (ii) An ∞-category X is minimal if any two J-equivalent simplices are equal.
- HMDEND-C07-S1-03.r1b | S1
  ATOM: Two $n$-simplices in an ∞-category $X$ are J-equivalent if, viewed as maps $\Delta[n]\to X$, they agree on $\partial\Delta[n]$ and are J-homotopic relative to $\partial\Delta[n]$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0218-s01] Definition 5.58 (i) Two n-simplices x and y in an ∞-category X are said to be
    [HMDEND-p0218-s02] J-equivalent if, when viewed as maps ∆[n] →X, they agree on ∂∆[n] and are J-homotopic relative to ∂∆[n].
- HMDEND-C07-S2-01.r1a | S2
  ATOM: Let $p:X\to S$ and $q:Y\to S$ be minimal J-fibrations between ∞-categories; then any fibrewise J-homotopy equivalence $\phi:X\to Y$ over $S$ is an isomorphism.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0224-s17] Proposition 5.70 Let p : X →S and q : Y →S be minimal J-fibrations between ∞-categories.
    [HMDEND-p0224-s18] Then any fibrewise J-homotopy equivalence ϕ : X →Y over S is an isomorphism.
- HMDEND-C07-S2-01.r1b | S2
  ATOM: For minimal Kan fibrations between general simplicial sets, any fibrewise homotopy equivalence over the base is an isomorphism.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0224-s18] Then any fibrewise J-homotopy equivalence ϕ : X →Y over S is an isomorphism.
    [HMDEND-p0224-s19] The same is true for minimal Kan fibrations between general simplicial sets.
- HMDEND-C07-S2-02.r1a | S2
  ATOM: For a J-fibration $p: X\to S$ between ∞-operads with $X$ normal, there exists a minimal J-fibration $q: M\to S$ that is a fibrewise J-deformation retract of $X\to S$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0275-s04] Theorem 6.56 Let p : X →S be a J-fibration between ∞-operads.
    [HMDEND-p0275-s05] If X is normal, then there exists a minimal J-fibration q : M →S which is a fibrewise J-deformation retract of X →S.
- HMDEND-C07-S2-02.r1b | S2
  ATOM: For a J-fibration $p: X\to S$ between ∞-operads with $X$ normal, if $S$ is also normal, then the retraction $r: X\to M$ onto the minimal J-fibration $M\to S$ is a trivial fibration.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0275-s04] Theorem 6.56 Let p : X →S be a J-fibration between ∞-operads.
    [HMDEND-p0275-s05] If X is normal, then there exists a minimal J-fibration q : M →S which is a fibrewise J-deformation retract of X →S.
    [HMDEND-p0275-s06] If S is also normal, then the retraction r : X →M is a trivial fibration.
- HMDEND-C07-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: If $p : X\to S$ is a minimal J-fibration between ∞-categories and $f,g : T\to S$ are J-homotopic maps from an ∞-category $T$, then the pullbacks $f^*p$ and $g^*p$ are isomorphic minimal J-fibrations over $T$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0225-s13] Proposition 5.73 Let p : X →S be a minimal J-fibration between ∞-categories.
    [HMDEND-p0225-s14] If
    [HMDEND-p0225-s15] f, g : T →S are two J-homotopic maps from an ∞-category T, then the pullbacks f ∗p and g∗p are isomorphic minimal J-fibrations over T.
- HMDEND-C07-S3-01.r1 | S3
  ATOM: For minimal J-fibrations $p: X \to S$ and $q: Y \to S$ between ∞-operads with both $X$ and $Y$ normal, any fibrewise J-homotopy equivalence $X \to Y$ over $S$ is an isomorphism.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0273-s19] Proposition 6.54 Let p : X →S and q : Y →S be minimal J-fibrations between ∞-operads and suppose both X and Y are normal.
    [HMDEND-p0273-s20] Then any fibrewise J-homotopy equivalence X →Y over S is an isomorphism.
- HMDEND-C07-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: The stricter dendroidal notion of minimality, which demands $x=y$ instead of $\alpha^*x=y$ for some tree automorphism $\alpha$, is described as less useful in practice, since the more general automorphism-based notion is needed for the existence result for minimal deformation retracts.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0273-s13] Of course there is an alternative to (b) in which one demands x and y to be equal,
    [HMDEND-p0273-s15] However, this stricter notion turns out to be less useful in practice.
    [HMDEND-p0273-s16] In particular, we need the more general notion to have a result such as Theorem 6.56 below.
- HMDEND-C07-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: In the dendroidal setting, minimality of a J-fibration is defined by requiring fibrewise J-equivalent dendrices to be related by a tree automorphism rather than to be equal, because the stricter equality-based notion is less useful in practice and the more general notion is needed for the existence of minimal deformation retracts.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0273-s13] Of course there is an alternative to (b) in which one demands x and y to be equal,
    [HMDEND-p0273-s14] rather than related by an automorphism.
    [HMDEND-p0273-s15] However, this stricter notion turns out to be less useful in practice.
    [HMDEND-p0273-s16] In particular, we need the more general notion to have a result such as Theorem 6.56 below.
